utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber has considered to give some more guidance on procedural matters to the parties. We will do that, not today, but we prepared a -- we are preparing some more guidance in respect of several aspects. Such, for example, I will just give an example is that we give Defence guidance as to whether they have to specify what documents will have to be -- whether they have to indicate through which witness they will introduce documents, also the specific documents and not just the list in respect of a number of witnesses. But you will have to wait for one or two more days. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am in the process of drafting a motion in respect of the oral order that was handed down by the Trial Chamber on the 30th of October, last Tuesday. That's the oral order that concerned the banking system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If the guidelines which have been prepared by the Trial Chamber at the moment will touch upon time allowed for cross-examination, then I can do one of two things. I can either ensure that that is indeed filed tomorrow, if it is of any assistance, alternatively, wait until those guidelines are given and then we can consider our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think that the -- let me just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not expect any further guidance as to the banking system, just time to be used by the parties. So if you intend to submit to the Chamber further thoughts in this respect, you perhaps better not wait. Yes. Then I think that we could continue with the examination of the witness. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You still can hear me in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. And then, Mr. Stamp, please continue the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were attached to the 120-millimetre mortar crew in Sarajevo, were there any other mortar or artillery units that were attached to your brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the brigade, there was also the Sokolac, the Sokolac mortar battery. So that means that there were three battalions, the Rogatica battalion, and my battery, the Sokolac one, and I think also the Pijesak one, it didn't have a separate battery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Sokolac battalion have mortars or artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning, there were 120-millimetre mortars, the same battery, and on -- upon the transferred to Petrovici, they also got some mountain cannons, after war production, I don't know what the type was, I think 48 or something. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any batteries of 76-millimetre field guns?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the battery of 76-millimetre field guns located?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located behind these two 120-millimetre mortar batteries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "behind," you mean to the south of the 120-millimetre batteries at Petrovici?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were each -- well, were there 82-millimetre mortars assigned to each battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. We didn't have 82-millimetre. Only later, three mortars came so just before we went to Petrovici. But within the companies, each company had two, that is, one 60-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that among your targets -- or is it your evidence -- may I withdraw that. Is it your evidence that while you were at Ivanici among your targets were ABiH forces in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also ABiH forces on the other side of the Miljacka river in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, around the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times, approximately, I can imagine you can only be approximate on this, approximately how many times were you ordered to fire on these ABiH units?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was on several occasions. Sometimes fightings went on for two days. I remember that once we refrained from responding, from returning fire. It was a Muslim attack on the Jewish cemetery. And the fighting went on for a whole day. And it was only in the evening that we fired and the attack ceased in the course of the night. And this happened on countless occasions, during every Muslim attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those occasions, is it your evidence that they were firing at the ABiH lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in a way, the way that the question is asked, I am not sure that it is comprehensible. This "they" puzzles me somewhat in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will rephrase it. I think I said "you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those countless occasions is it your evidence that you and your mortar battery were firing at the ABiH lines?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that as being their lines. Very frequently they would attack in three waves on to our lines which were located alongside the confrontation lines, that is, the barricades dating from the month of April, which means that we were firing on them, on the first front lines that they were attacking. We didn't fire on their defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the distance between the lines, their front line and the Serbian Army, the Bosnian Serb Army front lines in the vicinity of the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, and also in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery, while you were there were very close, not more than 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in certain places there was just a wall of a building, of the same building, and there were lines that were very close, even under 15 metres, less than 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, therefore, that when you were firing at them in the circumstances, you would have to be very careful that you did not hit your own troops; is that so? You would have to exercise caution not to hit your own troops?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite normal, and it is -- it was logical that we would -- we would take that into account in order not to hit our own troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take into consideration the weather conditions as they Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were at the time you were ordered to fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. And the time of the firing, whether it was day or night, particularly at night one had to be very accurate because it is very hard to adjust the sight then to target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive meteorological reports in respect of the weather conditions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, no, no, not to that extent, no. You know, it was war, that's what we had to do. It was war. It wasn't an exercise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you take into account the weather conditions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the situation that we saw, that we observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you make observations and allowances for the wind speed and wind direction?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, not so frequently. Personally, I tried to make all the calculations from the schedules and normally once whenever accuracy was needed, I would conduct all the calculations, estimations. But, of course, there were shifts as well. And I said that I was the only one in that battery who had the right military specialty for this. I was the one who was the mortar operator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that you would make all the calculations from the schedules, by "schedules" I take it you mean the mortar firing tables?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The calculation is done in two ways. We had a professor of maths who was a good -- who could calculate well from the tables. And then there was another way, doing it according to a planchette, which is a French system dating from the end of last century. We didn't have contemporary systems for calculations like American systems using a calculator, using a computer. We couldn't have that amount of accuracy, that degree of accuracy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, did you not earlier, that it was normal to fire into the city, notwithstanding that there were civilians living there, in response to enemy fire. When you fired into the city --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that -- I am sorry. I believe that in the confrontation lines there were no civilians. We withdrew our civilians, that's a fact. They were not directly on the demarcation line, on the separation line. And my belief is that in that part where the Muslim targets were, there were no civilians, except if someone was crazy enough or that they had a need to leave the civilians there, to position them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you fire at any time into the city itself away from the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was talking about the parts from which they fired artillery, where they had intense concentration of their own forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it your answer is yes, you did fire into the city, away from the confrontation lines; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that sense. There was the confrontation line and where they use their artillery from. As far as I am concerned, or they were preparing an infantry attack, as it was the case in the settlement, in the emptied school in Buca Potok, as I already mentioned or around the Viktor Bubanj Barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now saying that you never fired into the city in any area where there might have been civilians residing, living?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. This is much too general question because we don't know where civilians could have or could have not resided. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The question may be answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't fire at civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fire into the city, away from the confrontation lines where civilians might have lived at any time?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Was there a requirement that you record the targets that you shot at and whether or not you succeeded in hitting those targets? And when I say "record" I mean record in writing.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Particularly later on, because UNPROFOR representatives arrived and we had to have this kind of data and before as well, we had a register, a logbook which is made in every department which fired, and then also on the level of a platoon. Which means that this in this logbook we kept the azimuth of the main direction, the elevation, and other data that is important. Occasionally we didn't have the return information, if it was not a guided firing. I said myself that we ourselves did not determine what the targets were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just ask the Chamber if it is possible, this is democratic institution, I would like to address it. I don't know if this is normal for you, this is ordinary for you. But these little papers that Mr. Prosecutor is getting and that contain falsehoods, lies, misinformation that were going around, I believe that this method isn't correct in a democratic institution. Because perhaps then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "little papers"? I do not see any little papers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the right-hand side, the gentleman, that is what he did last Friday. All the time he has been have having these pieces of paper in front of him with false names and all this, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from giving your judgment on what is on papers that you have never seen. The Prosecution is working as a team. They can assist each other, and in order not to interrupt unnecessarily, they might communicate, just as I do with the Registry, by means of small notes. May I invite you to answer the questions put to you and not to comment on the way the Prosecution operates. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, last time, two names were confused, when Slavko Aleksic was asked about. There was Vasko's name, another man's name from a completely different part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I instructed you to answer the questions and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One question about that, Mr. Golic: Over the last couple of days, have you seen any piece of paper with any falsehoods about you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I invited the witness not to comment and not to interfere with the Prosecution operates. I think it would not be of great assistance for the Chamber to ask the witness about pieces of paper of which, at least, as far as I know, he cannot have any knowledge as to what is on these pieces of paper. Please proceed. Or do you have any specific issue you would like to touch upon and then perhaps you better explain that in the absence of the witness. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I did -- he did answer the question I asked. The answer is not on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't finish my answer. I was asked about a chimney. I never said that, and that was also a question from the piece of paper about putting a shell down a chimney stack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you are speaking about the pieces of paper exchanged by members of the Prosecution team to which you have no access. Is that correct? Then, it is not an issue you would have to comment upon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these records that you kept in respect to your firing of the mortars, how long were you required to keep them?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not kept for very long, these records. They were in some -- this was a logbook from the former JNA and sometimes it was for myself and the battery that I kept it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a requirement that you keep a record of the shots that you fired for the purposes of examination or investigation by the artillery commander?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know I remember once there was an investigation, Mr. Grajic came, so fortunately we had everything. It was handed over to him. He was the chief of artillery and he asked us to hand this over to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any requirement that you provide these records to the artillery commander or any superior officer on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the battery commander, on the whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The investigation that you spoke of in which you had to deliver the records to the artillery commander, when was that investigation? You recall the month?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in June. A mortar shell fell behind our lines and that matter was investigated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that is June 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "a mortar shell fell behind your lines" were there any casualties as a result of this mortar shell which fell behind your lines?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one of our men was slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any other investigations conducted by your artillery commander or any superior officer of your brigade in respect to misfiring of mortars or possible misfiring of mortars?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of any such investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated -- withdrawn. Is it your evidence that from your vantage points on the prominent positions at Vraca you could see the front lines at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. You couldn't see the demarcation line in the entire area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the buildings in Grbavica in the area of the front lines from Vraca?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the whole, you could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course from Vraca you could make out the height of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often were you told by superiors not to fire at civilians and to obey the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the battery is concerned, Mr. Grajic, the artillery chief, usually did this. And I remember he lined up both batteries and then read out those orders, perhaps we didn't even have the occasion to act contrary to these instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often were you told this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe every 10 to 15 days. It depended on the need. There was other information regarding the situation at the front, and above all regarding the situation in Rogatica, where we came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In the months while you were posted to Sarajevo did you receive leave from duty occasionally?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spent 40 days there at the most without having leave, but the shifts took place every seven days, usually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during some of those times of leave did you return to Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return there on or around the 22nd to the 25th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say right now. Sometimes I regret not having kept a diary, that errors are made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part in an attack by the Bosnian Serb Army in Rogatica in May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object. This doesn't seem to be within the territorial framework and is outside of the chronological scope which is referred to in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, can you respond or should we ask the witness to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness be allowed to step out, just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please ask the witness to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question posed and just a few other questions I might have, subsequent to that question, are not questions aimed to elicit information, generally speaking, about events outside of the time or area of the indictment but elicit information about the conduct of the witness himself and go to the credibility of the witness and might assist the court in evaluating the evidence which the witness gives. But they are not generally about or the purpose is not to elicit information outside but about the conduct of this witness in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain to us why this specific subject would cast a -- would assist the Chamber in assessing the credibility of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The questions would tend or seek to elicit information about whether or not he was involved in shelling of other areas and what were the consequences of those shellings, if so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what do you mean, following orders or not following orders or? It is still not clear to me whether how --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness has testified that he has not heard of any situation in which the RS Army was involved in any breach of military discipline or any breach of law, military law. I think that is the expression he used or was used by counsel when counsel asked the question. The questions go to his credibility about whether he or his units were present and involved in various breaches of military law, contrary to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you could listen to us with regard to information that the Prosecution has provided?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You objected --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... respond. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, there are two things. First of all, the place mentioned by the Prosecution is very far from Sarajevo and has absolutely nothing to do with Sarajevo. It is not even certain that at the time it was within the SRK, that's the first thing. The second thing is that even if such-and-such a person may have done, committed acts before the period, this has nothing to do, and we have already had this problem with a zone, an area to the north of Sarajevo, the area of Breza, and I am appealing to the jurisprudence of your Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the previous decisions of your Chamber

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... testify whether the answer given previously is credible, and if he would establish that the witness himself participated in such violations, as far as I understand, then you would say the answer is not credible. To this limited extent, but really to this limited extent, we will allow you these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, did you participate in an attack by the Bosnian Serb Army in Rogatica in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in an attack. At the time I don't think that the conflicts had even started. It wasn't until the 15th of May that there was the first casualty. When we went there, we didn't join any kind of formations. We quite simply rested at home. I didn't participate, for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you present at any time in 1992 when Bosnian Serb military units were involved in fighting in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... allowed you your objection, and I think the answer of the witness that he rested at home at that time should make you move to your next subject, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your -- I beg your pardon. Was your unit involved in the attack on Gorazde in the summer of 1994?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the same objection. The same objection. I am expressing this objection as a chiasmus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained, unless you would -- please proceed, Mr. Stamp. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to take advantage of this opportunity to find out how much time the Prosecution has because we have said that it would take half an hour and I think this time has been used up already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, that is, could you give us an indication?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are a few areas in which I would like to explore more comprehensively. But having regard to the time limit, I will try to complete this cross-examination very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what means "very shortly" because half an hour was more than half an hour as well. Five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will do it within five minutes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire of the Court in respect of the previous ruling, does the ruling mean in effect that no questions can be asked about the presence of the witness at Gorazde, Gorazde, I beg your pardon, or his activities there or that particular question is not permitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I would say that your understanding is right, that the Chamber deems the presence of the witness in Gorazde insufficiently relevant to continue that line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that as time passed during your sojourn in Sarajevo, you began to receive ammunition, shells, which were not of the best quality or you said words to that effect; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to identify those shells by looking at them?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question -- well, it's been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you fired those shells, would the possible error occur by it overshooting the mark or going short of the mark or deviating left or right of the mark?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you had to take care with regard to the distance, in general. For example, heavy mortars, M-48 mortars, mortar shells which were about -- which weigh about 17 kilos, if everything was all right in the firing tables, well those sudden problems with these items and you had to use less elevation for a greater range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the identifying features of the -- of these shells?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the shape and the weight, the shape of the detonator, the packaging of the detonator. In some cases, the detonators were not inverted so it was -- this is something that could be determined very easily, even at night, without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you fired these shells whether at day or at night, would you use them in situations where your own troops might have been near to the target? And when I say "near," I say within 100 to 200 metres to the target, would you use those potentially inferior shells?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that later on we didn't shell as frequently, that those shells would arrive when we were in the Petrovici territory and our targets were in general in the areas of Obranici, Colina Kapa, Zlatiste and in the direction of the Jewish cemetery. So our units were only near the Jewish cemetery. Nothing else was within our range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the quality of those shells improve over time?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit that we would receive all sorts of things. There were shells with foreign production. I remember that there were certain inscriptions in the Hebrew language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they improve --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the quality of the shells improve over time?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were firing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not for me to decide on this, but if we say five minutes, that means five minutes. There are other witnesses who are waiting and we don't want to have the same problem as last time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I say five minutes, I will keep an eye on the clock, and as the Defence usually did not interfere 30 seconds after such things had happened, I would invite you not to do it as well. Please put your last question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had targets which were close to, and that is within 200 metres of where your troops, your own troops were positioned, would you use shells that you recognised as inferior or possibly defective to fire at those targets?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used what we had at hand at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Is there any need to re-examine the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Half a dozen questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, my first question is to clarify something. Do you remember the sort of train, this wagon, this compartment you described on which a mortar had been mounted?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have the impression that in the transcript something has not been entered. You mentioned two men. Where were those two men with regard to that compartment, to that train compartment?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. If I mentioned it, I don't remember mentioning it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will put the question differently. Who operated the weapons on that railway truck?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I saw the men who operated it, and I don't know how this railway truck moved. I said that you couldn't see the locomotive Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but that the railway truck, the railway compartment was moving. I think that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking about the weapons and not about the train compartment itself. Did you see the men who operated the weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another series of questions. You spoke about a lorry that had been adapted to serve as platform from which a weapon could be fired. It was a Fap, 13-ton Fap, do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Serbian translation, an F-A-P, a 13-ton Fap.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it weighs about 13 tons, but the load it can take is 7 tons. That's the size of the motor, 1.300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the men who operated the weapons on that lorry?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was at a distance. We saw them operating, but it was not possible to see how many men there were. You know, someone drove the lorry for sure, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. If you saw them operating, could you tell us whether they were wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That question, not only appears to be leading, but the objection is primarily that it does not arise out of cross-examination and is not permissible to raise it as re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Faps, first, were discussed early in the morning of last Friday during the examination-in-chief. Is there any reason why you could not have put those questions in respect of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite that but in cross-examination there was a series of questions in relation to the lorry, to the way that it came out, the way it went in, and I recall that there was a line of questioning, precise questions, with respect to where the tunnel was located. There was a confusion, it seems to be, with the Kosevo Hospital and the Kosevo tunnel and I wanted to clarify these points. So about the precise location, and also to find out whether one was able to see uniforms on these vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we will allow you to a very limited extent one or two questions in this respect. Uniforms is not something that came up during the examination-in-chief. Your question was not about -- yes, your question was about uniforms and you justified your questions by primarily telling us about locations. So to a limited extent, you may put one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Including the question of uniforms, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one question about uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please tell the Chamber how the people who were operating these weapons were dressed?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Vraca, you couldn't see very well, to be honest. Frequently them and us, we mostly wore the old uniforms of the former army, but we all wore what we had. So neither army was ever fully dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Second question: When you spoke to us about the tunnel, could you give the name of the tunnel again so that we are sure what we are talking about? The question is: Do you know whether in this tunnel there were other weapons apart from the Fap 13/7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That again does not arise as to whether there are more weapons or less weapons. That is something the Defence should have explored in chief if it is relevant to his case. That issue did not rise in cross-examination and it cannot be raised in re-examination. We submit that the question is not permissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked the witness during examination-in-chief about mobile mortars firing from the tunnel and also other weaponry from that location. So it seems that you were the one who did put questions similar like the one you are putting now to the witness in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The reason why I asked this question is the following: There was a line of questioning asked by Mr. Stamp about the fact, to find out about a tank attack, whether there was attacking a tank with a shell, that was something that could be done. And I wanted to explore certain things on Friday and your Chamber told me that I could not. And now I just wanted to raise a number of questions in relation to these tank attacks, particularly if they are -- they were located where we think they were located, these attacks on tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I recall, the evidence from cross-examination, all that was asked was a hypothetical question about whether or not it would be efficient or effective to fire the mortar at the tank. The evidence of the witness was that he received orders in respect of firing at tanks, at least once. Again, therefore, what my friend proposes or the area he proposes to enter could not arise in re-examination. However, if he is permitted to raise these new issues, I would ask for the time to cross-examine him on whatever is brought out by my friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained and the matter has been dealt with in examination-in-chief and does not arise from cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, a question in relation to what appeared in cross-examination, these logbooks where you noted your targets and the hits, when the representatives of the United Nations came to visit your battery, were you in a position to give them the data that you had in your logbooks? If you can answer with a yes or no, I would appreciate it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me personally, battery commander, yes with the presence of the chief of artillery, but not me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if this battery commander had done this in fact?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard, Witness, of any protests that may have been done with the United Nations force that had to do with your own firing from the battery that you were commander; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear, Witness, anything whatsoever in relation to hypothetical protestations that may have happened for the same facts, but not in relation to your battery, but in relation to much more important hierarchy, for instance, the battalion; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The previous question was outside the scope of re-examination and so is this one. It didn't arise in cross-examination and he is going into new grounds as a protest. As a matter of fact, the issue of the presence of United Nations personnel arose in chief, firstly in chief. If there were matters involving protests that the Defence was interested in, it could have been inquired about at that time. It does not arise from cross-examination. May it please you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it seems that you take the logbooks as a starting point for questions about what could have been done with the information contained in the logbook. Yes, but that's, of course, not -- that would re-open the examination-in-chief as a whole, because let's just assume that everything was noted down in the logbook. So you have put a few questions, although they did not arise directly in the cross-examination. Unless there is a clearer link with the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. cross-examination, I would invite you to move to your next subject. May I also remind you that half a dozen is six in my view, but since two or three might be more as well, could you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We share the same notions, Mr. President. The clearest link is the following: During the cross-examination, the witness spoke of the existence of an investigation which was conducted by the chief of artillery with respect to one specific incident. It seems that these logbooks may have been used to show what had happened during the investigation, and this investigation was mentioned in the cross-examination. What I am doing, I am just using it instead of asking about Mr. Grajic, I believe, and an internal investigation, I just want to ask questions about a parallel level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two more questions, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the witness has already answered, I am just going to ask one more question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this subject, do you know if any protest was made by UN forces on the level of your battalion, and if you can answer with a yes or no, we would appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Very last question with respect to the quality of the shells, do you know if on the other side the shells were of a different quality, or were they --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We asked no questions about the shells from the other side. It doesn't arise from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put this question to the witness, and that will be the last one, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if on the other side the BH forces had the same problems with their own weapons in terms of quality of shells, that is, on the quality of firing as well and the quality of firing?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now the question not only does not arise, it is now very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a leading question. Please answer the question and we will hear what your answer is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I shouldn't have had the second part of the question, I would have answered to it that they were not very precise. Sometimes they even used the anti-hail shells, you know, the very heavy sound which is very frightening and doesn't have good precision. They were very unselective and very unprecise in their firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your last question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You spoke about two tanks dug in near to the Kosevo tunnel. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above. That is, on the slope which goes from the Hum hill towards the old Ciglana, it is not populated there. But it certainly -- it is just soil there. It is not populated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Do you know whether those tanks ever fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I did not see it. I don't think I said I did, but it was from our men on the positions primarily who were located in Vraca. I heard that that is where the firing was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: How far is the nearest entrance to the Kosevo tunnel to the nearest building of the Kosevo Hospital complex, if you know?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say on the left-hand side. From the west side there was a lorry that came -- the mortars came -- fired from the lorry. And from the Kosevo Hospital, it was mostly during truce periods, there was 10 or 15 such examples. So the question has nothing to do with the operation from the mobile trucks. Perhaps I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The question is: The distance, the distance between the Kosevo tunnel and the Kosevo Hospital, which is the distance? It is very simple. The hospital is a very big complex. I am talking about the closest building to the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps some 400 metres. There is an entire road between them and goes to Vogosca near the Kosevo stadium. It has nothing to do with each other, the Kosevo tunnel and the Kosevo Hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Were your mortars fixed to the ground or could you move them from their place? I am sorry. I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were fixed to the ground, but we also moved them because a mortar, if there were 10 or 15 shells, if that -- if the soil is soft, then it starts sinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions for you. JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] I would like you to tell me about -- clarify two or three points for me, please. The first is in relation to the tanks. If I recall correctly, you said, and I am going to quote you in English, it was an answer to a Prosecution question [In English] "The tanks were dug in, and you could only fire with shells which had fuses." [Interpretation] If I understand well, to a question asked by Judge Nieto-Navia, you said that you heard, that you didn't see, the tank. Were you speaking of one single tank? Were there several tanks? And where do you have this information that the tanks were dug in, in fact?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- not that I didn't say the tank. What I mean is that I didn't see the tank fire which is a completely different thing. I didn't see the tank fire. But we did see tanks dug in. We saw the barrels come out. I didn't say without a detonator, but only with delayed det -- time delay detonators. So they would be detonators with a time delay built in. And I said that instantly highly explosive shells there would be no point in doing this. I don't know. We didn't use those. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So what you are saying, what you are saying is that you saw the tanks dug in. In English, it was "dug in" --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said in my first testimony on Friday, I believe. That's the truth. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. But they were immobile targets, they were immobilised in a way?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, my second question: You said, and I am going to quote you in English [In English] "I was the only one in the battery who had the right military specialty for this." [Interpretation] And can we understand that during your absence, or while when you were not there, your battery continued anyway to function. Who was taking over from you, if the person who was in charge was not capable acting as a qualified military person?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the others were not -- didn't have the expertise, but I said that within a very short period from the 13th to the 28th of March, the battery in the area of Han Pijesak and in the training firing in Kalinovik, we became capable for conditions very quickly and the commander officer of the battery, late Jovan Orasanin, had been an infantry lieutenant and he knew how to operate the 82 millimetre mortars, and his deputy, Milorad Krajisnik from Rogatica, served on M-48 mortars, the so-called heavy mortars which had wheels. So all of them managed to become good at this, good at operating in a very short period of time. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Well, you said, if I understand correctly, to a question that was asked, and I am Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. going to quote the question in English [In English] "Battery crew used map coordinates to fire," [Interpretation] You answered and I am going to quote [In English] "At the time the map you cannot see the height of the buildings." [Interpretation] So what do you do then? How were you able to take into consideration the buildings, different heights of buildings, without hitting some nonmilitary targets? How do you handle this problem of different heights of buildings, of civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question was within the context of another question, and I think that's the reason why I went around the lines to see where we were able to operate, where we were able to fire. That is precisely why we couldn't fire when we were asked to, what you just said, Judge, is if there was another battery which was in a possibility to hit this target. So if I am firing with a mortar behind a high building, and there is a target, and obviously I cannot hit that target if there is a building in front of it, so sometimes we would have to go personally and see which targets were possible. We didn't fire the targets that we -- you just said -- we didn't fire the targets that we couldn't hit. It is not a question of height, but it was a question of where the shell was supposed to go to from where the point -- the point from where the enemy forces were firing, if I understood your question correctly. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. I am just quoting you. These are not my words. So another thing, please, you said that you intervened in terms of -- if there was an attack, that is, you returned fire when there was a Muslim attack. I understand well that these were infantry attacks. Could you perhaps explain to me how a mortar can intervene, how can it be engaged when there are troops, when there is manpower that is engaged? Don't you risk -- isn't there a risk of hitting your own troops with mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For these reasons that's why I said we fired towards the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, Jewish cemetery, those locations when there are no high buildings. Where there are high buildings, the mortar is not much use. So we didn't fire alongside the river bank and so on. Naturally with the first shell, there is always a factor of risk and that a shell is then sent somewhat further away. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So you're saying that to be very accurate you have to fire more than one shell?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Golic, I've got a few questions for you as well. Is my understanding correct that you and your battery were operating in the beginning of 1993 as well?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the Sarajevo area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then. That's not a correct understanding. Thank you for that answer. As far as the tanks are concerned, we -- you have answered several questions in respect of these tanks that were dug in. You told us Friday that you could only see the barrels on the south-eastern slope of Hum towards Ciglana, and that's what you told us today as well. The matter came up subsequent to a question about firing of mortars from the Kosevo tunnel. Could you tell us, these tanks, were they dug in westerly from the Kosevo tunnel or easterly?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: North-west. Somewhat further away and further towards the west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what distance, approximately, from the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps some 800 metres because the tunnel is little lower down and the other is further up towards the hill. So it is very hard to say because it is a slope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand you well that this is also, therefore, seen from the tunnel, not in the direction of the Kosevo Hospital, but in the other direction?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you told us that sometimes if you wanted to hit targets, especially if they were hidden more or less by buildings, that you would have to go and look and see whether you could identify these targets. Could you give me examples of that? What would you see if you tried to identify them?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said from Vraca you could see the memorial park and what I didn't say, nobody asked me about it, they had their anti-aircraft cannon at 220 millimetres and from that place you could observe the best. Most of the time the targets from high buildings, as I said, where some sniper firing, where you could only hear the hit, the shot much later because the sound doesn't travel so well. And you can -- don't know whether the bullet has been fired or not. But these were not our targets and we simply could not target such sniper nests. We mostly targeted locations of concentration of the Jihad Army, their artillery positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was your unit ever involved in responding to sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, we were not in a position to do that. I am sorry. In terms of Mojmilo hill, from that part located above where Lukavica was and the Mojmilo hill, there are settlements when the Sandjak people were and there on several occasions -- I apologise -- we did operate. But this was like the suburbs and around in the hills, they had their positions as well. So it was their line, their position, as well as the snipers in some basements or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then respond to, how would you consider this? Was this only if there was an attempt for a breakthrough or that you would be involved in such an action?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Breaking the Muslim line through. I didn't take part in such an operation but as a battery we took part in the liberation of Zlatiste. That is the part below the Trebevic, where the Muslim had a direct link to Skenderija where there was a secret tunnel or something and they came out from there. This was held by the police and the police handed it over to the Muslims. So we couldn't use that road and we had to lift the blockade and sometime in June, in the first attack, we didn't manage to take Zlatiste, and in the second attempt, the second attack where our battery was also engaged, I think there were five platoons with six weapons and all the shells, so I think that was -- and then Zlatiste was taken.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not platoons, but salvo. Interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answer. This concludes your testimony in this court unless there are any --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just three areas that I would like to ask about briefly, but I don't know if my friend, if the Defence would have any. I think the order would be for them to go first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I always try to say to the witness, "this concludes the evidence" but I now and then hope that that would be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is provocation, Mr. President. I will leave this to Mr. Stamp, and we will see what we shall do subsequently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will do that anyhow after the break if these are more than one questions -- yes, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, let me just first -- I think the proper order to proceed is to ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin whether he wants to put any additional questions, and he indicated more or less that he would wait and see. But I think it would be proper that you make up your mind now whether you have any additional questions to the witness, if so, please put them to the witness, and if not I will ask Mr. Stamp to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, perhaps just one question. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Further re-examination by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you spoke about, in response to a question put to you by the President, you spoke about the tank that had been dug in. And the question is as follows there will be two questions. The first question: Was this tank operated -- accompanied by its operators, the troops that are supposed to use it usually; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw it, I didn't see anyone moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Secondly, the position, the place where the tank was dug in, did that prevent the turret from rotating? Did it prevent it from making the rotations that tank usually makes when it is in action?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I know is there was shelling of our command in Vraca. It didn't rotate, but I think it was possible for it to rotate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the only thing I asked is where the tanks were located, especially whether they were west or east of the tunnel. That is the only clarification I sought. And I see that you are now touching upon different matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But let me explain why, perhaps. You asked whether it was while going away from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I wanted to say is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to make sure, could this have been said when the witness is present or -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think so. This doesn't concern me directly. But what I wanted to establish was whether it was possible for a tank, whether it is west or north-west with regard to a certain spot, whether it is possible for it to fire over such a position which could have provoked fire in response. This is the only thing I wanted to establish and I think that the witness has answered the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if that was your last question. I do not see it, as a matter of fact -- yes. "When I saw it, I didn't see anyone moving. Yes, being dug in would not prevent the turret from moving." Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said in answer to Judge El Mahdi that a mortar tube or weapon cannot fire over a building. May I ask you this: Is it not possible for a mortar round because of its relatively steep angle of descent to hit a target which is behind a building?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't that, that if the building is high it can't fire behind the building. It has its trajectory, a shell has its trajectory so it can't hit something behind a tall building. Just because the building is very tall and the shell has its normal ballistics trajectory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that it is impossible for a mortar shell to hit a target behind a tall building or would it depend on the distance between the target and the tall building?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. If the distance is great from the place where the shot is fired from, then the angle of descent is lesser and the area behind the building that can be hit becomes reduced, if I have understood your question correctly. We never fired at a distance closer than 2 to 3.000 metres except when we had semi-direct firing in the Mojmilo area, when we aimed directly, all the targets were over 3.000 metres away. And regardless of how high the shell goes, it can't hit something behind a tall building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You also said, if my understanding is correct, that you can't fire at something you couldn't see. Is that your evidence or is it that many times observers --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So it is correct that you would be able to fire at targets which you couldn't see with the direction of your observers? Or may I rephrase that. Is that with the assistance of observers telling you exactly where the target is your mortar battery could fire at targets which you couldn't actually see from where the mortars were placed?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said also that in respect to firing in the vicinity of Brotherhood and Unity Bridge and with the Jewish cemetery you said that with the first shell there was a factor of risk and that shell is then sent somewhere further away. What do you mean by that? When you say the first shell would be sent somewhat further away, do you mean that it would be sent further away from targets, perhaps your own troops that you did not want to hit?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Mr. President, the last question with your leave is in respect to a new issue which was raised by my learned colleague for the Defence in re-examination. And that is in respect to the battery commander showing to UNPROFOR personnel the logbook or the records of firing. So it doesn't really arise from a question that was asked by Your Honours, but something which arose, and it is one question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that you thought that your battery commander might have showed your battery's logbook of firing and targeting to United Nations' personnel. Can you say what were the possible reasons or circumstances why your battery commander might have showed this logbook to United Nations' personnel?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When representatives, UNPROFORs -- when UNPROFOR representatives would go around, this was mostly in Petrovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The circumstances in which your battery commander might have showed the UNPROFOR personnel the logbooks were merely when they visited?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Golic -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not a question, but quite simply the witness mentioned the Dobrovoljacka Street. I don't know if we could ask the witness whether this concerns the same street that is sometimes called the Benevolencija Street, and this is just so as to be able to establish what we are talking about. I am told that it is not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, it would have been proper to ask the witness whether he knows whether this street also has another name, because it was leading; and second, I do understand that you received an answer to your question from a different side. So there is no need to answer that question any more. Mr. Golic, it took us quite some time but you finally now have answered all the questions of the parties and of the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We also know that it is quite a distance where you come from. We would like to thank you for having come to The Hague and have testified in this court because this Chamber needs the information given by those who have been present at the relevant times and at the relevant places. Therefore, thank you once again and I wish you a safe trip home again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no documents that are in need to be admitted into evidence. It is still a bit unclear to the Chamber at this very moment who would be your next witness, and if it is a witness that you asked -- for which you sought protective measures, and let me just try to make things clear. It is a woman or it is a man? That might clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is a man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it is a bit confusing to me. Let's just turn into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anyone in the public gallery? We can't see it from here quite well. There is no one in the public gallery. We then turn into open session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration of which the text will be handed out to you now by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. We will not use your own name, but we will use the pseudonym -- Ms. Pilipovic? We will use the pseudonym DP11 and your face will not be visible for the outside world as well since protective measures have been granted in respect of you. You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed. Do we have to turn into private session or...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, very briefly just to get biographical data from Mr. DP11, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you told us that after the war broke out you moved to Vraca, to Grbavica, in Novo Sarajevo municipality. Can you tell us, in September of 1992, were you in that area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when you say that you were in that area were you engaged anywhere?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that you were engaged in the Army of Republika Srpska, can you tell us in September 1992, did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity -- I withdraw that. Could you tell us what was the unit that you belonged to in September 1992 as a private, as a soldier of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3rd company, 3rd Battalion of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters corrects herself, 4th Battalion of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, how many people were in the battalion of your 3rd company [sic]?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many? What was the strength of it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on what was happening in the terrain, the composition of the unit changed. Normally it would be 80 to 100 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what kind of weapons you personally had and in terms of your unit?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an M-84 rifle, and the company had automatic rifles, automatic and semi-automatic rifles, two machine-guns, and two mortars, M-60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, 80 to 100 people who were a part of your company, who were these people?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were ordinary citizens of the settlement, of the neighbourhood where we lived. Average age of the company was about 45.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you have a uniform and if you did, what kind of uniforms did you have?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To start with, we did not. But later on, beginning of 1993, we started receiving some uniforms. Later on, somewhat more. Camouflage, ordinary camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in September of 1992, where were the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning from the beginning of April until the end of 1995, these positions were held the same in the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was the commanding officer of your unit?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mirko Stanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your company was part of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was the commander officer of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know to which brigade your battalion belonged to?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the 1st Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us who the commanding officer of your company was and who was the commanding officer of the battalion, could you tell us whether these people were professional soldiers or were they also citizens who lived in that area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanding officer of the company was an ordinary citizen who lived in that area. The commanding officer of the battalion was in the or had been in the Yugoslav Army before the war and had the rank of a captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, could you tell us about the length of the front line of your company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. About 250 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where were you stationed while you were on the front line?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a house nearby in Pandurevica about 30 metres from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that in this house was the command post of your company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you were in the positions, so from the period from April until 1995, you say this line didn't change, this position didn't change, and that two members --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is a mistake. It is from April 1992 from 1995 until the Dayton Agreement was signed. Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you are telling us that from April 1992 until the end of 1995 you were with your company holding these positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, did you dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you tell us that you dug trenches, are you telling us that during the duration of the conflict and you spent time in these trenches and the war you spent time in the trenches?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the positions of your company, the front lines for which you say were on the Jewish cemetery, can you tell us whether in the vicinity there were BH Army soldiers, and if so, at which distance were they in relation to your front line?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the lower part by the chapel of the Jewish cemetery, about 50, 60 metres away. And the top of the cemetery, they were at a distance of about 30 metres on the other side of the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you're telling us that the lines of separation of both armies in relation to the Jewish cemetery were at the Jewish cemetery?
