utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one side of the wall of the Jewish cemetery, we were. On the other side, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show one part of the Sarajevo map to the witness DP11 considering that during the -- by answering some questions he told us about the positions of his company. And we would like to ask the witness to mark the positions of the company and, if he knows, of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be D1778.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP11, on your right-hand side do you recognise a map? You can have a look on your right-hand side. You can have a look at the map.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. DP11, if you can, could you please mark with a black pen the positions of your company. Just a moment. Just a moment. If you can use a fine-liner, please, so that... If you can just tell us what you are marking at this moment so that we can say it into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] My 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- could you mark for us the positions of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks] That's the 4th Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are marking the positions of the 4th Company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many companies were in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the positions of the other companies?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks] 5th Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've marked the 3rd, the 4th and the 5th. What about the positions of the 1st and the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 1st company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Positions of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. D11, in relation to the positions of the battalion, and specifically your company, could you mark, indicate, the front line of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, if you can use a dotted line to indicate the positions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps if he could use a dotted line, but a blue marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A blue marker would suggest that it was done on the request of the Prosecution, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we usually do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not use the blue marker --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. And just for clarity, sic, I am wondering if the witness would be able to explain what he means when he marks lines, in response to questions about the position. If he meant these were the front lines of the companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems there could be some confusion in that respect. Could you please clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you indicated the part of the companies that were part of your battalion, could you tell us the area of the 4th Company, what part of town is that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the position below the main road in the direction of Pale going towards the Vrbanja Bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the location and the part of town where your 3rd Company was?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position of your 3rd Company, what part of town is that? You said it was the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jewish cemetery. I said it was Jewish cemetery, I said it several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position of the 5th Company?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the location, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 1st company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st company's position were in Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague told me that what was not entered into the transcript was the answer of the witness about the positions of the 5th Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, could you tell us precisely about the positions of the 5th Company, what part of town is that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Below the Debelo Brdo, former barracks of the JNA Bosut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say former barracks of the JNA, could you tell us what army used that barracks before?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commanding officer of the company Vojvoda, Slavko Aleksic. It was composed of ordinary people and it belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the position of the 1st Company, what positions were they as part of the positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were positions below Staro Brdo and around Staro Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "below Staro Brdo and around Staro Brdo," can you tell us what is the altitude of Staro Brdo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 750 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the positions of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part is that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the road going towards Pale, Zlatiste, via Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you marked the positions of the companies within the 3rd Battalion, can you mark on the map the front lines of the BH Army and use a dotted line for that, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which colour?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With a black fine liner, dotted line, please. And if we can be efficient, please, and could you tell us which parts of town you are now marking?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am marking here below the 4th company where are the positions of the Muslim army [marks]. In front of the 3rd Company, Muslim lines [marks]. And then I am marking in front of the 5th Company [marks], and then in front of the 1st Company [marks], and then in front of the 2nd Company [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what the purpose is, but if these markings are going to be of any use, precise use later on, we need to have a record of what he is saying in reference to what he is writing. As he drew the lines, both set of lines, he has been explaining without us being given a description of what he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, there might be some confusion. The last dotted lines the witness has drawn which he said that -- let me just -- of which he said that these were the lines, the front lines of the BH Army. He testified that was -- he was marking the lines below the 4th Company, and he drew the line from the Miljacka river close to a number, "292," and close where it reads "Unioninvest" in south-easterly direction passing by as it seems the Jewish cemetery, if I am correct, and then the dotted line continues over what is Staro Brdo, and then turns into an easterly direction. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, by marking these lines, the dotted ones as well as the full lines, did you mark the positions of the two armies?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will explain it a little. I will elaborate a little. I marked it so that there is no confusion regarding the changing of the line because there was no change to the line during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. D11, you're telling us that these lines, the way that you have marked them, are dotted as being BH Army lines, and full lines as being lines of the positions of the Republika Srpska Army were the front lines which were in position throughout the conflict period? Are you confirming then that from April 1992 until the end of the war in 1995, these were the lines?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the start of the war until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, since you've marked these lines, could you tell us what period of time from the time when they were set up until the end of the war, what period of time did you spend on these positions of your 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the start to finish. From 1992 until the end of 1995, that is, until the company was disbanded and Serbs left Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you've marked these lines, can you tell us, from the period of 1992 until September until the 10th of August 1994, in this area that you have marked, was there fighting?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was intense fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the fighting was intense, could you tell us how frequent such fighting -- how frequently such fighting occurred?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you say that the fighting occurred on a daily basis. But can you tell us whether you had personal knowledge as to the positions from which the fighting was being fought?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They fired at us from the direction of Hum. They fired at us from tanks. They fired at us from Pofalici where the water supply system is. They fired from multiple rocket launchers at us. From the railway station, they fired at us with mortars. And from the tunnel which goes towards the Kosevo stadium, they fired at us from a tank. From the Kosevo Hospital they fired at us. They fired at us with mortars. They fired at us with snipers from all the high buildings, including Mojmilo, the Assembly, the Executive Committee, the Marshal Tito Barracks, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you listed the positions of the BH Army and the positions from which they fired and the weapons that they used, can you indicate the Sogbunar and Sirokaca [Realtime transcript read in error "Rogatica"] positions on this map?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, Witness, could you mark the place that you have called Sogbunar with a number "1."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Use number "2" to mark the position, to mark Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to avoid a misunderstanding, where the question -- the earlier question reads the Rogatica positions, I think you asked then already for the Sogbunar positions. I think that is page --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I don't know how Rogatica turned up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you marked with number 1 the place called Sogbunar and Sirokaca with number 2, now that you have done that, can you tell us with regard to those positions from which you said the BH Army fired at you, could you tell us what weapons, what guns were used in the fighting and how often were they used?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They used mortars almost on a daily basis when they would attack us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "mortars," are you claiming that they only used mortars or were other weapons used?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was heavy infantry weapons, Pams, PATs, machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, do you know whether in those areas, the areas of Sogbunar and Sirokaca do you know when the members of the BH Army were positioned? And if you know, what unit was there?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were located in the school and Caco's units and the Black Swans led them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, just for the sake of the transcript, I can see "Pam" and "Pat." Perhaps it would be a good time to clarify this. It is PAN, instead of Pan and it would be necessary to say what a "Pat" means. We know what it means, but this is so that everyone can know what it means. If you like I can tell you. I will be quite happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we should ask the witness to clarify and I think it is --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you said P-A-M, Pam, and P-A-T, Pat, if that is what you said?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pam. That's a 12.7 millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what these abbreviations mean?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you indicated the Sogbunar and Sirokaca positions and told us that these were the BH Army positions, can you tell us that whether from the position where your company was located, did you move from those positions? Did you go to other positions that your battalion had?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. You have made a mistake. These weren't the positions of the Muslim army, but of the Muslim artillery. And these were positions where they had other weapons too. But the Muslim army was by the Jewish cemetery, by the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. D11, that's how I understood you, but I wanted to know whether you and your company went to other positions that your battalion held?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I went there personally. I went to help the 5th Company, the 2nd Company, the 1st Company, when there was fierce fighting, when a fierce offensive had been launched. I could provide you with the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you say large-scale offensive or large-scale attack, could you tell us when this took place?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was mostly at the beginning of April 1992 and in June 1992, December 1992, January 1994, 1993 February, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, when you said "December 1992" could you tell us what period that was, in December 1992 and could you tell us what the nature of the attack was?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the first half of December. There was a large-scale attack at the Jewish cemetery. They were all intense. All the attacks were intense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you told us that you and your company, you personally and your company, were present at all the positions held by the other companies, that is to say, by your battalion. Could you tell us the position of your 1st Company with regard to the positions that have been marked, and with regard to the BH Army positions? So from which parts of the town could be best seen from those positions?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all parts of the town in the Old Town, Grbavica, Vraca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you were in that position, could you explain us to what the positions of the BH Army were with regard to Staro Brdo?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the French UNPROFOR forces arrived, the Muslims took up position in the -- among the rocks of the Staro Brdo behind the barracks, the Bosut barracks, and they fired at us from the flank, they fired at our units of the 3rd and 4th Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the positions of your battalion, and when you mark the positions in the Staro Brdo, can you tell us which other positions were dominant with regard to the town?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which were controlled by the army?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army controlled Mojmilo, Zuc, Igman, Debelo Brdo, above Vogosca. Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the Colina Kapa positions? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslims had Colina Kapa under their control. They fired at the road to Pale via Trebevic, there was sniper fire, they came under sniper fire and it was shelled by artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, the Defence would like -- Defence counsel would like to show a photograph to the witness, the number is 341, and we would like to tender this document into evidence under this number. Because this number has been mentioned in the list of evidence as 341D. And our colleagues from the Prosecution have these items.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, can you recognise the view that you can see in this photograph? Does it mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us from which positions this photograph was taken, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the left side of the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the high -- the tall white building, could you tell us what this building is?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute, Witness. You said that the white building that is prominent in this photograph is the Executive Council building, have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate this building to us once more.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said the Assembly building, for the sake of the transcript, when you -- it's the white building with a black roof which is just below the Executive Council building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness pointed to this building and said it was the Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, can you tell us whether you can recognise any other buildings in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript the witness has pointed to a yellow building on the left-hand side, to the left of the Executive Council building and he has said this is the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Hum, and it is the relay station on Hum.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any other buildings in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, when the witness indicated Hum building with the relay station, he pointed at the hill in the background with the tower on top of it on this photograph. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was just wondering whether it would be necessary for the witness to encircle the buildings and indicate what they are with a number to indicate the Assembly building and Executive Council building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark the Executive Council building with a number "1." You can make a large circle. You can encircle the building and you can mark it with a large number "1."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Presidency building, can you mark the Presidency building with a number "2" and encircle it. The Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, the yellow building which is to the left of the Executive Council building, can you encircle that building and mark it with a number "3." That is the Holiday Inn building.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, you said that the Hum hill and relay station, you said that this was number 4. Could you mark a large circle there too, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Number "5," the railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've marked the railway station with a number "5." Could you tell us about the building which is at the foot of the railway station which has been marked number "5," what sort of building is that? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the Marshal Tito Barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark that building with number "6." Could you mark the Marshal Tito Barracks with number "6."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, are there any other buildings that you can recognise in this photograph? Any other buildings that you were able to see, any other building that you can see in this photograph and that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see all of these tall buildings here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, could you tell us between the Holiday Inn building that has been marked with number "3" and the Marshal Tito Barracks, do you recognise the building between these two buildings?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the transport school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark the transport school with the number "7."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, in the course of 1992, from March 1992 until the end of the war, until August 1994, do you personally know whether during that period these buildings were used by BH Army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which of these buildings that you have marked with the numbers, 1, 2, 3, 5 --

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will take them in order. Number 1, sniper nests. They fired at Vraca, the Jewish cemetery, Grbavica. Number 2, also sniper nests, targeted the Jewish cemetery and the road to Vraca. Number 3, again, sniper nests. Number 4, multiple rocket launchers fired from there. Number 5, mortars and snipers. Number 6, snipers. Number 7, that's where they fired at the tunnel. That's from where tank fired. And these buildings were used for accommodation for the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, in the course of 1992 and 1994, can you tell us whether and how often soldiers fired from the positions that you have marked and with the weapons that you have mentioned? How often did this occur?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this occurred on a daily basis. Several times every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness showed the witness a photograph, D331. Defence would like to show the witness another photograph marked D331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we proceed, can I inquire if there is a lighting system on the ELMO? Perhaps the photograph could be illuminated a little bit more than it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please see whether you could make it even more... Perhaps we could continue meanwhile since we all have a photograph in front of us. It is the best possible result, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, can you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you can see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the entrance to the Jewish cemetery from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to this entrance that you say is the entrance to the Jewish cemetery, can you tell us which forces had it under their control in the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the control of the BH Army throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this would be a good time to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn until five minutes past 6.00 but not until after Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps my observation could wait -- would await the adjournment. Perhaps what I would like to indicate could await our return to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not follow you. Yes. You would say you tell me after the break. Yes. We will adjourn until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the issue you wanted to raise, is that something that can be done in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is something which I think I ought to reserve and allow the flow of evidence. Instead of introducing a procedural matter at this stage, I think I will observe it at a more appropriate stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D11, on this photograph you told us that Jewish cemetery could be seen. This was the entrance to the Jewish cemetery. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous photograph you showed us some buildings that you recognised and for which you told us where the buildings that during the conflict were held by the BH Army. Could you tell us, from the positions of the Jewish cemetery, what view did you have in relation to these parts of town, that is, to the locations that we marked?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a very good view because these were tall buildings. And we were on an elevated point, higher than 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, my colleague would continue with the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon. Witness, good afternoon. Earlier you spoke of the positions located on what we call Colina Kapa. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if there are several Colina Kapa locations?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this name, Colina Kapa, is there a qualifier to indicate something?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know. Very well. Witness, do you know if the positions of Colina Kapa in relation to your own positions, in relation to the positions that you held, were they to the south or to the north or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of which army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the positions of the BH Army on Colina Kapa. Was this in front of you or behind you in relation to the city that you had in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the position of Colina Kapa, was this between you and the city; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness an exhibit, one of the Prosecution maps. For us it will be number 1779, and could it be pleased placed on the ELMO. I suggest that we place the document in colour on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you please focus on the two lines, the line which is dark green line which is located at the south of the map, and that is the VRS; and the light green, which is in the north of this map above Brajkovac, would correspond to the BH Army positions. This position of the lines at the time, did they seem accurate to you; yes or no, and why?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you see a circle, a red circle below point 58?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. According to your experience, which one of the two armies at the time that you knew was located in the area marked by this red circle?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you absolutely certain about this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, between the circle that you mentioned and number 2, do we see, or rather what do we see between those points in terms of facilities, buildings or obstacles? What do you know about this space between?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a locality held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can withdraw this map now and we can go on to the next map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As it is being withdrawn, may I just note for the record that there was a summary provided and reference was not made to the fact that this witness would be testifying in respect of incident 2, sniping incident 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as this is concerned, I am not sure -- I will have to check the correspondence, what has been submitted, and then I will check it later. Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... informed before the -- before 7.00. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will just confer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Map 180 with the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, again, we have a map. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The positions of the lines, do they seem correct to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The last observation I made in respect of notice from summaries, I again make in respect of this map, for what it is worth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is incident 11 mentioned in the summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is the same answer, I believe, because we are going to check and we will tell you later, if you give us your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Questions had been answered already when Mr. Stamp raised the issue in respect of the -- of the earlier questions. We are now about to hear the answers of the witness. Will there be any different questions to -- in respect of this map compared the earlier one or would you -- do you intend to ask the same to the witness? Because the first question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If the question is addressed to me, then I will answer. The questions that we would like to ask are in relation to the proximity of the cemetery, what is known as the Jewish cemetery in relation to this incident and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether there is any additional summary, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but I see 12, 15 and 24 on your summary. This is not a minor issue you are raising here in respect of -- let's just first concentrate on sniping incident 2. It would have been appropriate to, if you indicate incidents in your summary, you cannot in view of the questions you just put to this witness leave out number 2, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we will check, with your leave, as soon as possible, precisely this question of the testimony. I don't know whether this is in the correspondence of the 29th or the 30th of October that we were referring to. It could be in one of these letters. I don't have them before me, Mr. President. Mr. Stamp, whether this witness, I don't recall it, but was this witness mentioned in the letter dated the 29th of October, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are 2 and 11 mentioned in that letter Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 28th of October. We have two summaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the last summary, discuss it indicate 2 and 11?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. 12, 15 and 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it before me. I will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the incidents are not mentioned in relation to sniping incident 2, then it seems that the Defence has disregarded the rulings of the Chamber in respect of these incidents. The Chamber will consider what we will have to do. I mean, the questions in respect of incident 2 have been put to the witness. Are your next questions in relation to incident 11 or more general on the area? The positions at the Jewish cemetery have been mentioned in the summary, already in the first summary, so you are allowed to ask questions in that respect. But the Chamber, again, stresses that we will not just continue this way. I mean, this issue has been raised several times. The Defence has been ordered not only to give further details as to what are relevant facts in relation to certain sniping incidents, but now, as far as at least as we can establish at this very moment, even not the specific incidents are mentioned, especially in respect of incident number 2. It cannot be said that this is not of importance for the Prosecution in preparing for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to say that the Defence specified every incident in the submission that my colleague sent last week. I think it was last week. It was in French, written by my colleague. I think it was mentioned at the meeting that we had with you. I believe this is a misunderstanding, but unfortunately I do not have the letter that is in French with me now, because I did not know it was going to be contested. It was all mentioned in there, which incidents we mentioned with which witnesses. I believe this is a slight misunderstanding now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I could not check this at this very moment. Mr. Stamp, if relevant facts in respect of incident 2 and 11 have been mentioned in recent correspondence, it would have been inappropriate to raise the issue, as you have done it. We will check what has happened. We will check what is in the correspondence, and then we will see who is to be blamed for what happened here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will now proceed in the following fashion, please. I propose that the witness tells us for the map simply if he knows to which army did the red circle belong to, the area of the red circle that he has to the right on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the -- the map is the same as the other one. Yes, it is different --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. Almost the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now could you please do the same exercise, if this is possible, in relation to an exhibit that I will show you now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the counsel, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. This is 1781 with the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you identify the document that you have to your right, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in relation to this document and from -- no, I withdraw that. In the red circle that you have in the centre of the map, could you tell us, if you know, which army held this area?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am just going to first correct the positions of the BH Army. It didn't go that way, but it goes, it just went right behind the cemetery. This red circle is the chapel held by the BH Army, so the lines should go here. Perhaps, I could correct it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps I could just interrupt you. With a black pen, I would be very grateful if you could correct what you think should be corrected, if this line, so-called BH Army line, could you correct it. If it is VRS line, please, with a full line, and the BH Army with a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we proceed, may I just inquire through the Court, which maps are these which the witness is being shown? These maps I don't believe they are in evidence in this form. I believe a corrected version by a particular witness is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you -- I take it that the Defence wants to tender -- looking at the numbers they are assigning to these maps, I take it that they, on the basis of the maps that were originally disclosed, I think -- that's at least how I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They would be new exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They would be new exhibits, otherwise they would not need to have any numbers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please do this, what I have asked you. So, with a dotted line, the BH Army line; and with a full line, VRS line, if you have to make any modifications, of course.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, gladly. I will correct the mistake. The line of the BH Army. The line of the 3rd Company, my company. And this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us of a chapel -- could you wait, please. With a pointer, could you please point to where the chapel was.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact location of the chapel was here, this red circle here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please mark it with a number "1," a small number "1." Mark the chapel with number "1."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I mark it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it in Arabic numerals.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, please tell me, under whose control was this chapel? Which army controlled it?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you be sure of this? What personal knowledge did you have of this?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I know about this because I spent four years there. They all fired from infantry weapons at us. They fired from the chapel at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But when you say that you were there during the entire period, do you mean that they were there -- they were also there during that entire period?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can claim that for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, from the positions that you have on the left of this map, were you able to see anything at the level that has been indicated by number 24 on this map and why?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a building there. They acted from the inside. We didn't see that. All that we could see was the firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps my question wasn't quite clear. I'll reformulate it in two phases. Can you see the number "24" in the middle of the map?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From the positions that you held, what was it possible to see at the level of the ground or where you can see the number 24? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see some large buildings there. It was hidden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "hidden," was it totally hidden, partially hidden?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On our side it was concealed by the buildings from the positions of the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 30 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber would like to avoid whatever possible confusion. We would like to verify whether there could be any. May I ask you a question: If you look at this map, and if you look at number "24" you see that it points to what appears to be a red dot. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know what is there on the place of that red dot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it is, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the Jewish cemetery chapel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I mean, that's the red circle. But I am drawing your attention to the red dot. Could you please point at it on the map, first at number 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that red dot. Could you tell us -- yes, the dot you just pointed at. Could you tell us exactly what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a tram track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you said that you could not see number 24 from your positions, did you indicate that you could not see that part of the tram track or were you pointing at where you see the number "24" written on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 24 on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you see from your positions the tram track at that specific point where you find the red dot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were curtains. It was difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well if you say that you would have a view on where the tram track was, if there had been no curtains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On our side, there were curtains there, but it wasn't possible to see that because of the tall buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps my next question would be: How would you then know that there were curtains there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wasn't there myself. I said there were curtains in the direction of the tram track, but high buildings obstructed our vision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but how did you know that there were curtains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say number 24 itself, but here in the direction of Marijn Dvor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then let me just ask precisely. Could you not see the tram track specifically on the red dot location because of high buildings or because of curtains? So I am only asking you about that specific spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The high buildings with regard to number 24 in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the red dot, you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, in the pause, I found in our file a letter that we provided the Prosecution with and I said the witness that we are speaking about now will be testifying with regard to everything, with regard to the Jewish cemetery will testify with regards to everything that concerns the Jewish cemetery. And specifically with regard to that, the impossibility of vision, the frequence of shooting, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The letter I have not exactly here. If you could just give it to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is just one thing that hasn't been mentioned, number 11, and this is a mistake for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the first page here, Mr. President, if it is required. I have the first page of the correspondence, if it is necessary. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us about these buildings, in other words, you said that from your positions you weren't able to see point 24 because of the high buildings. As a result, was it possible to fire from your positions at the red dot, number 24; yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because there was shooting from the BH Army side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would like to change the subject now and deal with this very briefly. I would like to move on to a series of technical questions. What can you tell us about ricochets and about stray bullets in the course of an exchange of fire? Could you respond to this question very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever there was an attack and whenever there was intense firing, bullets would ricochet from the walls because the Jewish cemetery is surrounded by very high walls, two metres high. It is a concrete construction, very solid material. So naturally the bullets would go all over the place. And the terrain is on a slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know if on the other side of the town of Sarajevo there were particular positions where the enemy could produce weapons, munitions, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know of any particular places?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do because I lived in the war -- I lived in Sarajevo before the war. One of such places was Vaso Miskin Crni. I know that because shells would hit our positions and they had BH Army inscribed on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where this factory was located, please?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of Marijn Dvor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see it on the map, the one that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you encircle this location, mark it with number "2" and number "2" will refer to the weapons factory.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know of any other locations --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With reference to the location, just to move to the centre of the ELMO so we could follow it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we could see it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps you could mark that with a number -- that's fine. Thank you. Witness, do you know of any other places where there were similar installations, similar sights in the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see these places on the map?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we see it on the other map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we go into these places which counsel has led the witness into, could we first establish the basis of this knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please ask more specific to the basis of the knowledge for the witness during the conflict, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, s'il vous plait, M. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, thank you. Could we put the overall map of Sarajevo on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have knowledge of the other places where weapons were produced?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through Croats, Muslims and Serbs in Sarajevo, they told us about it. They would be present in our units. And through the shelling of our positions, through shells that didn't explode because they had been produced rapidly, and not all the components had been included.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you well when you say that you knew about this because of knowledge you obtained during the course of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can see it, I would like you to show us on the map that we will place in front of you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I get that number, please, the number of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you see this map?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see some of the sites that you mentioned a minute ago in this map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you first of all indicate these sites to us on the map.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What do why have there? Witness, could you tell us what is located at those two sites? You pointed to two sites. We will write it down later on. But what was there at these sites?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Energoinvest and the Vaso Miskin tools factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would be grateful if you could encircle these two sites. The first one that you pointed to.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just a minute, please. Just a minute. And the second one -- just a minute. I don't think we have a number on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it with a letter "A" in the little circle to the right?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That refers to the tools factory. And mark the Energoinvest building, I think that's what it is, with the letter "B."

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what was made at these two sites?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just correct something, please. At site "A" there was the number "2" there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But we can see, and we know what we are speaking about now. Thank you. Witness, what was produced at the site marked with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They produced mortar shells there and ammunition for infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the site marked with the letter "B"?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that site, rifle-launched grenades, mines, barrels for rifles, optical devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you spoke about rifle-launched grenades. Could you tell us what they are, exactly these notorious rifle-launched grenades?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are infantry weapons which fired from rifles with -- they were fired from an automatic or semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I am going to turn to the issue of material, physical destruction, and to the extent that you have knowledge of this in your area. Could you, first of all, tell us when such destruction took place, in what period?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you tell us where, in territorial terms, this destruction was concentrated the most?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire line and the Jewish cemetery settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, when you looked at the town from your positions, was it possible for you to see mosques; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, you could see the tops of mosques. There are mosques in Sarajevo -- there are over 200 mosques in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was: Whether you could see mosques from the positions that you held; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, did you receive any instructions to shell these mosques; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you receive any instructions to shell other buildings of a cultural or religious nature; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, now with regard to the issue of civilians. If you received any instructions, what sort of instructions did you receive with regard to the protection of the civilians at the time of war? Had you received any instructions? What sort of instructions did you receive? Can you tell us anything about this, please.

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We put civilians in an area which was outside the combat area, but there were some civilians who were not responsible and they returned home to take certain items, clothes, et cetera. Mothers didn't want to leave their sons, et cetera, so a lot of them became casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are talking about victims on the Serbian side now, I think, is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know about that side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, of course. But that wasn't really my question. Were you given instructions in your company that concerned opening fire and it concerned the necessary protection that civilians should be provided with?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't have any orders to fire on civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Am I to understand, for the sake of the translation, that your testimony is that you were ordered not to fire on civilians?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Those last two questions were leading. The penultimate one leading, and the last one, very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If you want to have things clarified, it is -- I have since many times told you that the clarification should not be by way of leading the witness. If you understand the answer to be, although it appear on the -- it does appear on the transcript as a different answer, then perhaps you could ask for further clarification, but not by saying, "what in your view, the answer should have been?" Or at least that is how you understood it to be the right answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, to the extent that you have answered my previous question, could you tell us how frequently, if that was the case, you were issued with such instructions, with such orders?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could explain this better. We received orders every three days or every five days. Soldiers came who were leaving Sarajevo, which was under the BH Army and they would come from other units and they would join our -- bring our company up to strength because men who were fit for military service had been wounded or had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But as far as instructions that you may have received, were these instructions given to you as frequently as the ones that you have been referring to or were they less frequent or more frequent?

utterances.speaker: IZO GOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depended on the need, on what was required at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am just going to confer with my colleague for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am looking at the clock, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have 10 minutes at the most now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For tomorrow, yes. Then we will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this courtroom. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just allow me to write down my last annotation. I can't do it outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thank you for your patience. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
